title: Why Did Chime Financial Stock Jump?
detail:
Why Did Chime Financial Stock Jump?
Trefis Team

PYPL

Chime Financial (CHYM) stock rose 78.7% over the year to November 17, 2026. The S&P 500 returned 11.3% over the same year. Chime's shares started that year at $18.45 and closed below that price in June. The latest quarterly report came on November 4, 2026, when Chime raised its revenue forecast for 2026. So when did the shares make most of that gain?

Most Of Chime Stock's Gain Came After June

The stock struggled through a weak spring before recording the bulk of its advance. Shares fell 12.5% on May 7, 2026, the day after Chime released its first-quarter report. They eventually closed at $16.44 on June 10, marking their lowest close of the past year.

From there they turned sharply higher. The biggest one-day gain, 20.6%, came on August 6. The day before, Chime reported second-quarter growth that beat expectations and raised its 2026 revenue forecast. The shares reached their highest close of the past year, $34.55, on September 9. The shares closed at $30.18 on November 5, the day after the latest report, up from $29.87. They ended at $32.97 on November 17, still below the September high. Chime's peers did not share the gain. Over the same dates, SoFi Technologies lost 47.2%, PayPal lost 5.1% and Ally Financial gained 2.4%.

Chime Went From Deep Losses To A Profit

Chime earned $48.0 million of operating income in the twelve months ended September 30, 2026. A year earlier, it had an operating loss of $1,013 million over the same span. The company also posted net income in each of the first three quarters of 2026. It had a net loss in the fourth quarter of 2025.

Lower stock-based pay sits inside that swing. The cost fell to $272 million in the latest twelve months, down from $1,012 million a year earlier.

Sales growth picked up at the same time. Revenue grew 24.8% from a year earlier in the first quarter of 2026 and 26.8% in the second. Third-quarter revenue rose 32.1% to $718 million. Management said its MyPay and Instant Loans products led a 52% rise in platform revenue that quarter.

Chime Still Holds Far More Cash Than Debt

Chime's balance sheet looks much as it did a year ago. The company held $1,183 million of cash and short-term investments at September 30, 2026, against $129 million of debt. A year earlier, it held $1,079 million against $138 million of debt. The cash grew even though Chime spent $300 million buying back its own shares over those twelve months.

That could change once Chime owns Stride Bank, its partner bank for more than seven years. Management said Chime would then hold its members' deposits itself. The deal still needs regulatory approval, and Chime expects it to close in the first half of 2027. Those deposits would be money Chime owes its members. So once the deal closes, cash against debt alone will no longer show Chime's full position.

A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on November 16, as Reuters reported that the exit of the founder of the world's most closely watched AI chipmaker as chief executive had soured enthusiasm for AI shares. The chipmaker's shares had just logged their longest weekly losing streak since October 2012, and a Reuters columnist wrote that investors have been warned about a possible market top, though timing one is nearly impossible.

The damage was heaviest in technology. Reuters reported that chipmakers fell between 3.5% and 5% in premarket trading on November 16, while server makers dropped as much as 5.1%. Since October 6, the S&P 500 technology sector has fallen 20% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor index has fallen 30%.

AI Selloff Leaves Beaten-Down Stocks in Focus

A selloff this deep tends to send investors looking for names that fell too far. Swissquote senior analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya warned that buyers of a hotly awaited AI developer's market debut later in the week may sell existing tech holdings to pay for it, so a strong debut might not lift every AI stock.

Readers sorting through the wreckage can look at which beaten-down AI stocks analysts still see rising 50% or morein one of our rankings.

Rate Hike Bets Add to the Pressure

Interest rates are pulling in the same direction. Reuters reported that markets fully price a rate hike in December after hotter-than-expected inflation data, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a 50-basis-point increase at about 8%. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy will likely need "several interest rate increases" before spring 2027 to restore price stability. Rate futures price in only about three 25-basis-point hikes by mid-2027.

Safe havens have not helped. Treasury yields are under pressure from rate-hike expectations and sticky inflation, gold fell below $4,000 to a one-year low, and the US dollar has been the main winner. Fed officials made 19 public appearances in one week after 20 the week before.

Some stocks have held up better than the rest. Our list of stocks trading near all-time highs that Wall Street still likesshows where analysts still see room to run.

Bank of America Global Research economists expect the minutes of the October Fed meeting to show a deeper split over holding rates than the 10-2 vote suggested. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was due to speak in San Francisco on November 16, and 2-year Treasury yields had just posted their largest weekly rise in over two years.

title: Target’s Shoppers Are Coming Back as Store Traffic Jumps 5% After Falling 2.2% a Year Ago. Can the Momentum Last?
detail:
Target’s Shoppers Are Coming Back as Store Traffic Jumps 5% After Falling 2.2% a Year Ago. Can the Momentum Last?
Jeremy Bowman, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 3:29 PM MST 4 min read
TGT
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

You may have missed it from all the attention on AI stocks this year, but Target (NYSE:TGT) is one of the best-performing stocks in the S&P 500.

The retail giant has jumped 74% year-to-date as it's put its earlier struggles behind it and returned to growth under new CEO Michael Fiddelke.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Target kept that momentum going in the third quarter as the stock jumped 6.7% Wednesday on another strong earnings report.

The retailer easily beat estimates on the top and bottom lines, as comparable sales jumped 5.6% on a 5% increase in traffic, showing shoppers are returning to its stores. That drove revenue up 7.1% to $27.07 billion, which topped the consensus at $26.54 billion.

The company's Fun 101 category, which includes products like toys, electronics, sports, and entertainment, delivered 27% growth. Beauty and food and beverage were also strong, up 9% and 7%, respectively. Target's non-retail business, including subscriptions like Target Circle 360, the Target+ marketplace, and its Roundel ad business, grew nearly 20%, showing the playbook that it's borrowed from Amazon and Walmart is paying off.

Further down the income statement, Target's gross margin rose 120 basis points to 29.4%, excluding a benefit from tariff refunds, as operating leverage from the increase in comparable sales helped drive gross margin improvement. Adjusted operating margin rose from 4.4% to 5.2%, excluding the tariff benefit, and adjusted earnings per share jumped from $1.78 to $2.65, or $2.15 excluding a $0.50 benefit from related tariff refunds, representing a 21% gain. That beat estimates at $2.07.

Target also raised its full-year revenue growth from 5% to 6%, and its adjusted EPS guidance from $9.90-$10.90 to $10.65-$11.40, which helps explain today's pop as well.

With Target stock nearly doubling this year, investors are clearly betting on a long-term recovery, but is the momentum sustainable? Let's take a look at what's going well for the company.

Image source: Getty Images.

What's working for Target

On some level, Target is benefiting from the low-hanging fruit in front of it after several years of underperforming its industry. The company is reclaiming lost market share with basic improvements like reducing out-of-stocks and investing more in labor and training to improve the sales experience. The strong comparable sales in part reflect the previous downturn in the business as the company recoups lost sales.

title: He Turned 73 This Year and Skipped His First RMD When the Market Was Tanking. The IRS Charges a 25% Excise Tax on Whatever He Should Have Withdrawn, Selloff or Rally

He Turned 73 This Year and Skipped His First RMD When the Market Was Tanking. The IRS Charges a 25% Excise Tax on Whatever He Should Have Withdrawn, Selloff or Rally
Gerelyn Terzo
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 2:33 PM MST 6 min read
^GSPC
Quick Read

The IRS fixed his 2026 RMD at about $45,000 regardless of market moves, and skipping it triggers a 25% excise tax.

Waiting until April 2027 stacks two RMDs into one tax year, risking a higher bracket, more taxable Social Security and Medicare IRMAA surcharges.

Missing the deadline still allows a penalty cut to 10% by correcting promptly, or a Form 5329 waiver request, though a waiver is unlikely.

The biggest 401k decisions tend to get made once and never revisited: when to roll it over, what to hold inside it, and when to start taking money out. That is exactly what the report: 401k & IRA Tips and Answers was created to address, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

He was born in 1953, turned 73 this year and has about $1.2 million in his 401(k).

sturti / E+ via Getty Images

The S&P 500 has fallen for four straight sessions as of November 17, so he has left his first required minimum distribution (RMD) alone and plans to sell after a bounce. The IRS ignores the market. His required amount was fixed before 2026 began, and any shortfall draws a 25% excise tax.

His 2026 Withdrawal Was Locked In Last December

The RMD equals the prior year-end balance divided by the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table divisor. At 73, that divisor is 26.5. On a $1.2 million balance, his 2026 RMD comes to about $45,283.

That figure holds whether the account drops 15% in a selloff or gains 15% in a rally. A downturn only makes the withdrawal a bigger share of what's left. Federal law sets the tax at 25% of the amount by which the minimum required distribution exceeds what was actually distributed. If he skips the full amount, he owes about $11,321, and that comes on top of ordinary income tax on the withdrawal itself.

For many Americans, funding a 401(k) only leads to more retirement questions. Should you roll your 401k into an IRA, and when? What's the tax impact if the rollover check gets made out to the wrong name? When do required withdrawals begin, and how much do you have to take?

Fisher Investments put the answers in one place. 401k & IRA Tips and Answers is free, and it covers rollovers, contribution limits, required withdrawals, and what actually belongs inside the account once the balance gets serious. Read More Here ›

------

April 1 Is Technically His Deadline, and Using It Can Cost Him

The first RMD gets a grace period. A 2026 first-year RMD can wait until April 1, 2027, so technically he hasn't missed anything yet. But his 2027 RMD is still due by December 31 of that year. Waiting means both withdrawals land in the same tax year.

U.S. stocks ended mixed Wednesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunging more than 560 points as healthcare stocks declined and Nvidia reversed an early rally despite reporting stronger-than-expected earnings.

The S&P 500 extended its losing streak to five sessions, its longest since June, as investors weighed the Federal Reserve's outlook for additional interest rate hikes. The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite managed to finish higher, reflecting a divided market ahead of Anthropic's anticipated stock market debut.

The Dow fell 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to close at 50,198.17, while the S&P 500 declined 16.90 points, or 0.23%, to 7,323.63.

The Nasdaq gained 101.50 points, or 0.42%, to finish at 24,429.88. The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies rose 12.44 points, or 0.46%, to 2,714.31.

Nvidia remained a major focus after the artificial intelligence chipmaker reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double its revenue from the same period last year.

According to Nvidia's earnings announcement Tuesday, revenue increased 103% year over year, supported by continued demand for the computing infrastructure powering artificial intelligence systems.

The company also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, offering investors another indication of strong demand for advanced AI chips.

However, Nvidia shares surrendered their early gains and closed 2.9% lower despite the earnings beat.

The reversal came as investors continued to assess Nvidia's leadership transition following Jensen Huang's departure and the sustainability of massive spending on AI infrastructure.

Other semiconductor stocks delivered mixed performances. Advanced Micro Devices advanced, while Intel and Micron Technology declined.

Wall Street's attention also turned to the Federal Reserve after minutes from its October policy meeting showed that officials expected further interest rate increases could be necessary to contain persistent inflation.

Minutes released Wednesday showed that almost all policymakers anticipated additional increases if the economy developed as expected.

Two participants also indicated that an increase larger than a quarter-percentage point could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data proved unfavorable.

The Fed held its benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75% to 4% in October, but officials remained concerned that inflation could prove more persistent than previously anticipated.

The minutes also revealed discussions about the economic consequences of rapidly expanding AI infrastructure investment, including its potential effects on prices and financial stability.

title: Where Will Palantir Stock Be in 1 Year?
detail:
Where Will Palantir Stock Be in 1 Year?
Jennifer Saibil, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 2:59 PM MST 4 min read
PLTR
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The artificial intelligence (AI) play still looks intact even as Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock plunges. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 is up 11% year to date, and the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC), which is heavily weighted toward AI right now, is up 11%. Both of these gains are impressive, considering that Nvidia stock, which is a major component of the index, is down more than 12%.

However, Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) is also down. It's lost 5% this year despite fantastic operating results, and it's still wildly expensive. Where could it be in one year?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Sovereign AI for enterprises

Palantir has been the poster child for AI stocks for years. Its groundbreaking AI platform helps companies analyze data to detect patterns and make decisions while keeping their information private.

What began as a program for the military and U.S. intelligence, including seed money from the CIA, has bloomed into a broad business serving all sectors. The company's AI platform (AIP), which is geared toward commercial organizations, is thriving, driving incredible growth for the whole company.

In the third quarter, total revenue increased 96% from the year-ago period, and U.S. commercial revenue was up 148%.

However, as AI continues to develop and handle more daily tasks, competition is creeping in, both from AI agents and competitors specifically in this space, like Databricks and Snowflake (NYSE:SNOW).

Palantir claims that its edge lies in its sovereignty, meaning clients keep their data private and proprietary. The results show that clients agree. They're seeing excellent results from the partnership, which is the main reason they're likely to stay, at least in the near term.

What could happen in a year?

Palantir stock is dropping for two distinct reasons even though it's growing like wildfire. One is the threat of competition as AI flourishes, and the other is the stock's premium price tag. It trades at 118 times trailing 12-month earnings and 59 times trailing 12-month sales, and it's the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 on a price-to-sales basis.

With that kind of price, there's little room for error or negative market sentiment for any reason.

In the third quarter, for example, U.S. commercial revenue growth dropped down the tiniest of notches from 149% last quarter, and total contract value increased 6%, down from 49%. These things matter when the valuation is as high as Palantir's.

title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 18: CoreWeave Slides as Nvidia's Blowout Earnings Fail to Ease Debt Concerns
detail:
Stock Market Today, Nov. 18: CoreWeave Slides as Nvidia's Blowout Earnings Fail to Ease Debt Concerns
RJ Fulton, The Motley Fool

NVDA
IREN
^GSPC
^IXIC

Trading disclosure

CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) fell 4.13% on Wednesday, November 18, closing at $47.83. Strong quarterly earnings from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) initially lifted CoreWeave shares in premarket trading, but those gains quickly evaporated as investors shifted their attention back to the company's substantial debt burden and ongoing financing needs. Despite booming demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, Wall Street remains increasingly concerned about the financial costs of sustaining that growth.

Trading volume reached 58.9 million shares, approximately 28% above its three-month daily average of 45.9 million. Despite recent selling pressure, CoreWeave shares remain up approximately 20% since the company's initial public offering in 2025.

How the markets moved today

The broader market delivered mixed results on Wednesday. The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 0.24% to 7,323, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) gained 0.42% to 24,430.

Despite modest strength in technology stocks, AI infrastructure providers remained under pressure. CoreWeave's peer IREN (NASDAQ:IREN) fell 3.61% to $15.24, underscoring growing investor concerns about the substantial capital requirements and financing costs associated with expanding AI computing capacity.

What this means for investors

It is clear that demand for AI infrastructure remains exceptionally strong. Last week, CoreWeave reported year-over-year revenue growth of 168% and raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to between $13 billion and $13.3 billion. However, the market's reaction to Nvidia's earnings suggests investors are becoming less concerned about the strength of AI demand and more concerned about the financial costs of meeting it.

CoreWeave is targeting profitability in 2028, leaving the company with a considerable period during which it must finance its expansion. With the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%, elevated borrowing costs present a significant headwind for a business that relies heavily on debt financing to acquire computing hardware and expand data center capacity.

Looking ahead, investors should pay particularly close attention to CoreWeave's financing arrangements, capital expenditures, and ability to convert contracted customer demand into cash flow. Long-term customer contracts and prepayments provide some financial stability, but the timing of those cash inflows relative to infrastructure spending remains critical.

While CoreWeave's revenue growth is impressive, the investment thesis increasingly depends on whether the company can generate sufficient returns on its substantial capital investments. Until there is greater visibility into sustainable profitability, strong revenue growth alone may not be enough to restore investor confidence.
